gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on a 16-inch MacBook Pro a one-cable 16-inch 2560x1600 120 Hz screen runs with its brightness capped (80% on the Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro per Macworld's Simon Jary, 75 on the UPERFECT 16-inch 120 Hz per The Camping Nerd) until a charger is plugged into the screen, and that the Float 2 Pro then passes back at most 65 W against the 140 W adapter Apple ships with every 16-inch MacBook Pro.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's Mac roundup and PCWorld's roundup, both read in full. Macworld lists '65W pass-through charging' as a Float 2 Pro pro but never sets it against the 16-inch MacBook Pro's 140 W adapter, and says nothing on the brightness cap, refresh rate on a Mac, or HDMI. PCWorld only advises buying USB-C with DisplayPort Alt Mode and Power Delivery, with no Mac generation, refresh or HDMI detail. ChatGPT's own answer warns generically not to assume pass-through can power a 16-inch Pro, but gives no wattage. RTINGS and TechRadar returned truncated bodies and seattlepi.com blocked the fetch, so those three were not compared.
decides: It confirms the pick rather than changing it. The three 16-inch MacBook Pro generations whose Apple spec pages were read (2021, 2023, 2024) have native DisplayPort over their Thunderbolt ports and drive at least two external displays, so one 2560x1600 120/144 Hz screen needs no display driver and the base-chip one-display limit does not apply. Apple tells users not to use HDMI for Adaptive Sync, so the USB-C cable is the path for a FreeSync screen such as the UPERFECT GR16EQ. The power pairing supports the Duex Float 2 Pro's segment: it is the only candidate with a named-reviewer-sourced pass-through figure (65 W), while The Camping Nerd found the UPERFECT 16-inch 120 Hz did not charge a MacBook Pro. Either way the page should tell the shopper to keep the 140 W adapter on MagSafe and to plug a 15 W or larger USB-C charger into the screen for full brightness.

findings.label: 16-inch MacBook Pro (2024, M4 Pro / M4 Max): video path and external display count
findings.value: Three Thunderbolt 5 (USB-C) ports with 'native DisplayPort 2.1 output over USB-C'; M4 Pro drives up to two external displays at 6K 60 Hz over Thunderbolt; HDMI supports one display at 8K 60 Hz or 4K 240 Hz
findings.source_title: MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2024) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's figures. One added screen on USB-C is inside the limit, so no display driver is needed for a DisplayPort Alt Mode monitor. Apple quotes 6K 60 Hz as the Thunderbolt ceiling and does not list a 2560x1600 120 Hz mode.

findings.label: 16-inch MacBook Pro (2023, M2 Pro / M2 Max): video path and external display count
findings.value: Thunderbolt 4 with 'native DisplayPort output over USB-C'; M2 Pro drives up to two external displays at 6K 60 Hz over Thunderbolt; HDMI supports one display at 8K 60 Hz or 4K 240 Hz
findings.source_title: MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2023) - Tech Specs - Apple Support

findings.label: 16-inch MacBook Pro (2021, M1 Pro / M1 Max): video path and HDMI limit
findings.value: Thunderbolt 4 with 'Native DisplayPort output over USB-C'; M1 Pro drives up to two external displays at 6K 60 Hz; HDMI is limited to 'one display with up to 4K resolution at 60Hz'
findings.source_title: MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2021) - Technical Specifications - Apple Support
findings.note: Generation breakpoint: Apple rates the 2021 HDMI port at 60 Hz and the 2023 and 2024 ports at up to 240 Hz (4K). Apple gives no 2560x1600 120 Hz figure for the 2021 HDMI port, so on a 2021 model the USB-C cable is the documented route to a high-refresh screen.

findings.label: Variable refresh (Adaptive Sync / FreeSync screens) on a Mac: connection Apple requires
findings.value: macOS Monterey 12 or later on any Apple-silicon Mac; connect to the Thunderbolt port with a Thunderbolt, USB-C or other DisplayPort cable; 'Do not use an HDMI cable or adapter'
findings.source_title: Use an Adaptive Sync external display with your Mac - Apple Support
findings.note: Page dated 2026-07-16. Turned on in System Settings > Displays > Refresh Rate (Variable or Adaptive) on macOS Ventura 13 or later. Apple warns it 'might produce a flickering or stuttering effect' outside games and video, and says to pick a fixed rate if so. Applies to FreeSync rows such as the UPERFECT GR16EQ.

findings.label: Power adapter Apple ships with the 16-inch MacBook Pro
findings.value: 140 W USB-C Power Adapter; 'Fast-charge capable with included 140W USB-C Power Adapter'; 100 Wh battery (2024 model)
findings.source_title: MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2024) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: The 2021 (https://support.apple.com/en-us/111901) and 2023 (https://support.apple.com/en-us/111838) pages state the same 140 W adapter. The 100 Wh figure was read on the 2024 page only.

findings.label: Power on one USB-C cable from a MacBook, and pass-through
findings.value: Draws 7.5 W from the MacBook in Limited Power Mode, which caps brightness at 80%; a PD USB-C charger of 15 W or more gives full brightness and prevents flickering; with a wall charger it passes back up to 65 W to the laptop
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro review: Portable screen that floats above your MacBook (Simon Jary, Macworld, 2025-12-16)
findings.note: Macworld's Simon Jary; the review names an M2 MacBook Pro as the connected Mac. Arithmetic: 65 W is 46% of the 140 W adapter, so through the screen a 16-inch MacBook Pro charges below Apple's fast-charge condition. 7.5 W is 7.5% of a 100 Wh battery per hour. No built-in battery.

findings.label: Cables in the box and which one a Mac needs
findings.value: USB-C cable plus HDMI to Mini HDMI cable; 'The USB-C cable should be all a Mac user requires'; two USB-C ports and one Mini HDMI on the screen
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro review (Simon Jary, Macworld)
findings.note: Macworld's Mac roundup (https://www.macworld.com/article/2836233/best-portable-monitors-for-mac.html, read 2026-11-26) lists this screen's connection as Mini HDMI only; the review describes both USB-C ports.

findings.label: Fit and attachment on a 16-inch MacBook Pro
findings.value: Four included magnets fix to the MacBook's lid; 'It works well without magnets, although it's not as stable in use or convenient when carried around'; 0.7 in thick, 2.9 lb (1.3 kg); 'mirrors the 16-inch display of the top-end MacBook Pro'
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro review (Simon Jary, Macworld)
findings.note: The fit statement is Macworld's, not Mobile Pixels' own range; the maker's page could not be opened today (see unsourced). The review does not say what refresh rate macOS offered.
